headline: Anthropic is investing $100 million in a new academy to train 10,000 engineers to build and run Claude-based AI projects inside companies by the end of 2027.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a company program with a clear plan, but results will not show until 2027 and it is Anthropic's own announcement.
importance_line: It aims to ease a shortage of people who can put AI to work inside big firms, which affects the engineers, their employers and Anthropic's customers, but it is Anthropic's own plan and the first certified engineers are not expected until early 2027.
summary: Business Insider reports that Anthropic announced Claude Frontier Academy on 2 Oct 2026, a $100 million program to train 10,000 engineers by the end of 2027, with first groups from firms including Accenture, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk. Trainees take a multi-day in-person course and then spend 12 weeks leading a real Claude project at their own employer, with the first certified engineers expected in early 2027.
notes: Original outlet CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/02/anthropic-to-invest-100-million-to-train-ai-engineer-talent.html) was blocked (HTTP 403); wrote from Business Insider's report and checked it against Anthropic's own announcement, so source and url are Business Insider's.
